h: I will make you a great nation

p: בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (סִטְרֵי תּוֹרָה עח עַמּוּד א) חָשַׁב שֶׁבַע בְּרָכוֹת:
In the holy Zohar (Sitrei Torah 78a) it enumerated seven blessings:
"'וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל' – הַאי בִּרְכָתָא חֲדָא וְכוּלֵי,
''And I will make you a great nation'—this is one blessing, etc.,
'וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ וְגוֹמֵר' – הָא שֶׁבַע".
'and in you shall all families be blessed, etc.'—behold, seven.'
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ מִסְפַּר שֶׁבַע הֵם כְּנֶגֶד שֶׁבַע הַמִּדּוֹת,
And wherever the number seven occurs, they correspond to the seven sefirotic attributes,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "שִׁבְעָה מִי יוֹדֵעַ וְכוּלֵי שִׁבְעָה יְמֵי שַׁבַּתָּא",
as is written: 'Who knows seven, etc., seven days of the week,'
וְהַמְּכֻוָּון שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּזְכַּר מִסְפַּר שֶׁבַע
and the meaning is that wherever the number seven is mentioned
הֵם כְּנֶגֶד שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית שֶׁהֵם שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת תַּחְתּוֹנִיּוֹת;
they correspond to the seven days of Creation which are the seven lower attributes;
וּכְנֶגֶד שֶׁבַע הַמִּדּוֹת – שִׁבְעָה רוֹעִים שֶׁהֵם מֶרְכָּבָה לְהַמִּדּוֹת,
and corresponding to the seven attributes are seven Shepherds who serve as the Chariot to these attributes,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּזֹהַר חָדָשׁ תּוֹלְדוֹת),
as written (in Zohar Chadash, Toldot),
וְכֵן הוּא סֵדֶר הַבְּרָכוֹת כָּאן.
and so is the exact order of the blessings here.

h: Becoming a Great Nation without Measure

p: "וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל" – הַיְינוּ בְּלֹא שִׁיעוּר,
''And I will make you a great nation'—meaning without measure,
שֶׁכֵּן מוֹרֶה לְשׁוֹן "גָּדוֹל",
for so the term 'great' (gadol) denotes,
וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ שֶׁזָּכָה בְּמִדָּתוֹ עַד כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן,
and it corresponds to Avraham our Father who elevated his attribute up to Keter Elyon,
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְאַבְרָהָם זָקֵן בָּא בַּיָּמִים",
as is stated: 'And Avraham was old, advanced in days,'
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: "בְּאִינּוּן יוֹמִין עִלָּאִין וְכוּלֵי",
and as the holy Zohar wrote: 'into those supernal days, etc.,'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר בְּמִדָּתוֹ שֶׁהִיא הָאַהֲבָה עַד הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ בְּג' רִאשׁוֹנוֹת.
meaning that he was refined in his attribute of Love up to its root in the three supernal head-sefirot.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Chayei Sara 24:1: ““Abraham was old, advanced in days, and the Lord had blessed Abraham in everything.” “Old” indicates one who has acquired wisdom: holiness is established in him, and he no longer needs restraints. This came to him after the Binding of Isaac, after he was circumcised and underwent ten trials such as no other creature in the world underwent. He changed from one opposite to the other, like a convert who must turn and change from one opposite to the other, having until then been accustomed to a way that was not good. So Abraham our father attained completeness and changed from his previous condition, when he had needed acts of service and restraint. Now holiness became established in him, so that he would no longer need those acts and restraints. A person can reach this level only gradually. This is what “advanced in days” indicates, within human apprehension, as the holy Zohar states: “Abraham was old, advanced in days … in those supernal days, in those known days ….” This is the teaching in the Six Orders: “Any town that has ascents and descents causes people to age at half their days.” The nature of this world is that, if a person walks on a level path slowly, he does not age at half his days. So too in words of Torah: a person reaches completeness only gradually. Sometimes he seems to himself to be on a great level; afterward he sees a lack in himself and thereby strengthens himself in serving God to repair that lack. This is like a rebuke, through which a person becomes stronger in words of Torah each time, until he reaches his essential completeness.”

sourceExcerpt.en: “Abraham was old, advanced in days, and the Lord had blessed Abraham in everything.” “Old” indicates one who has acquired wisdom: holiness is established in him, and he no longer needs restraints. This came to him after the Binding of Isaac, after he was circumcised and underwent ten trials such as no other creature in the world underwent. He changed from one opposite to the other, like a convert who must turn and change from one opposite to the other, having until then been accustomed to a way that was not good. So Abraham our father attained completeness and changed from his previous condition, when he had needed acts of service and restraint. Now holiness became established in him, so that he would no longer need those acts and restraints. A person can reach this level only gradually. This is what “advanced in days” indicates, within human apprehension, as the holy Zohar states: “Abraham was old, advanced in days … in those supernal days, in those known days ….” This is the teaching in the Six Orders: “Any town that has ascents and descents causes people to age at half their days.” The nature of this world is that, if a person walks on a level path slowly, he does not age at half his days. So too in words of Torah: a person reaches completeness only gradually. Sometimes he seems to himself to be on a great level; afterward he sees a lack in himself and thereby strengthens himself in serving God to repair that lack. This is like a rebuke, through which a person becomes stronger in words of Torah each time, until he reaches his essential completeness.

p: "וַאֲבָרֶכְךָ" – תְּרֵין, נֶגֶד יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
''And I will bless you'—the second, corresponding to Yitzchak our Father, peace be upon him,
שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ פַּחַד יִצְחָק,
whose attribute was the Fear of Yitzchak,
וְהַיְינוּ לְהִתְבָּרֵר בְּמִצְווֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ",
meaning to become refined in the negative prohibitions whose primary root is 'You shall have no other gods,'
וְהוּא לְהוֹרִיק הָרַע מִלֵּב כְּסִיל,
and this means emptying evil from the heart of folly,
לִהְיוֹת אִתְפַּנֵּי יֵצֶר הָרָע מִתַּמָּן.
so that the evil inclination is purged from there.
וְזֶה עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהוּא "הַרְבֵּה חָכְמָה" לְתַקֵּן "הַרְבֵּה כָּעַס".
And this is accomplished via the Oral Torah which represents 'much wisdom' to repair 'much anger.'
וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה נִקְרֵאת "בְּרָכָה",
And the Oral Torah is titled 'Blessing,'
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ סֵפֶר הַבָּהִיר שֶׁכָּתַב: "וּמְנָלָן שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה אִקְּרֵי בְּרָכָה וְכוּלֵי,
as written at the opening of Sefer HaBahir: 'And from where do we derive that the Torah is called blessing, etc.,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'יָם וְדָרוֹם יְרָשָׁה', וּכְתִיב: 'רְחָבָה מִנִּי יָם'", עַיֵּין שָׁם,
as it is stated: 'Possess the sea and the south,' and it is written: 'broader than the sea,' see there,
וְהַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
and this points specifically to the Oral Torah,
דְּהַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב מְנוּיָה וּסְפוּרָה אוֹתִיּוֹתֶיהָ.
since the Written Torah is counted and measured in its letters.

paragraphs.text: Sefer HaBahir 3: “[Rabbi Berechiah continued,] "And why does the Torah begin with [the letter] Bet? To start with a blessing [b'racha]. From this, we learn that the Torah is called a blessing, as it is said, 'Full [with the] blessing of YHVH, possess the sea and the south' (Deuteronomy 33:23). There is no sea other than Torah, as it is said, 'And broader than the sea' (Job 11:9). And what is 'Full with the blessing of God'? It means that every place that [the letter] Bet is said is the language of blessing. As we say, 'b'reishit'. And there is no beginning [ראשית] except wisdom, as it is said, 'The beginning [ראשית] of wisdom is the fear of YHVH' (Psalms 111:10). And there is no wisdom except [as the result of a] blessing, as it is said, 'And Elohim blessed Solomon,' and it is written, 'YHVH gave wisdom to Solomon' (1 Kings 5:26). This is comparable to a king that marries his daughter to his son and says to him [the son] at the wedding, 'Do with her as you will.'"”

sourceExcerpt.en: “‘I will bless you’—this is our saying, ‘God of Isaac’”: from the side of strength, Isaac’s level. He clarified matters in the world and broke through all concealments, returning all matters to the blessed God, joining them to their root, and recognizing that everything is His. From his attribute branches out all a person’s wealth and property: through his service and restraints it is called by his name, for through the labor of his hands he has merited God’s abundance. Since he serves God, overcomes his heart’s desire, and breaks through all concealments to join and attach all matters to their root, God says that the line of justice indeed requires the power of the root to be in the branches—in the creatures who serve Him. It is to be called by their name, as though they themselves accomplished all this through their handiwork. This is what “I will bless you” indicates, from the Talmudic expression for layering a plant: what was layered grew.

h: Yaakov and the Greatness of Avraham’s Name

p: "וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ" – נֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ,
''And I will make your name great'—corresponding to Yaakov our Father,
שֶׁהוּא פָּעַל שֶׁמִּטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה,
who effected that his bed was complete,
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ",
and this is why Scripture says: 'and I will make your name great,'
שֶׁאָז נִתְפַּשֵּׁט קְדֻשַּׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ מִדַּת גְּדוּלָּה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד,
for then the holiness of Avraham our Father—the attribute of Greatness—spread to endure forever,
"שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד",
'the lip of truth shall be established forever,'
שֶׁאָז כְּבָר יָצָא הַפְּסֹלֶת,
for by then the spiritual dross had been purged,
וְאָז נִתְבָּרֵר שֶׁגַּם אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה,
and then it was clarified that Avraham our Father's bed was likewise complete,
שֶׁעֵשָׂו וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל לֹא נֶחְשַׁב זַרְעוֹ,
since Eisav and Yishmael were not reckoned as his true seed,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיִצְחָק "וְלֹא כָּל יִצְחָק",
as written regarding Yitzchak: 'and not all of Yitzchak,'
וְאַחַר לֵידַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ גַּם אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק נִקְרְאוּ "יִשְׂרָאֵל",
and following the birth of Yaakov our Father, Avraham and Yitzchak were likewise designated 'Yisrael,'
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תּוֹלְדוֹת), וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּטָּתָם שְׁלֵימָה.
as written (Midrash Rabbah, beginning of Parashat Toldot), meaning that their bed was complete.
וְכֵן נִדְרָשׁ גַּם בַּגְּמָרָא (פְּסָחִים קיז עַמּוּד ב):
And so it is expounded in the Gemara (Pesachim 117b):
"'וְאֶעֶשְׂךָ לְגוֹי גָּדוֹל' – זֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים מָגֵן אַבְרָהָם;
''And I will make you a great nation'—this is why we recite 'Shield of Avraham';
'וַאֲבָרֶכְךָ' – זֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים אֱלֹהֵי יִצְחָק;
'and I will bless you'—this is why we say 'God of Yitzchak';
'וַאֲגַדְּלָה שְׁמֶךָ' – זֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב", עַיֵּין שָׁם,
'and I will make your name great'—this is why we say 'God of Yaakov,' see there,
וְהַמְּכֻוָּון גַּם כֵּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ.
and the inner intention is precisely as we explained.

h: The forefathers and the written and oral Torah

p: "וֶהְיֵה בְּרָכָה" – אַרְבַּע, נֶגֶד מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ,
''And you shall be a blessing'—four, corresponding to Moshe our Teacher,
דִּכְתִיב: "וְזֹאת הַבְּרָכָה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרַךְ מֹשֶׁה וְגוֹמֵר",
for it is written: 'And this is the blessing wherewith Moshe blessed, etc.,'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא פָּעַל לְהוֹפִיעַ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּכָל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
meaning that he operated to radiate words of Torah within every single Jew,
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "תּוֹרָה צִוָּה לָנוּ מֹשֶׁה מוֹרָשָׁה קְהִלַּת יַעֲקֹב",
as is stated: 'Moshe commanded us Torah, an inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov,'
וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט): "'קְהִלַּת יַנַּאי' אֵין כְּתִיב כָּאן אֶלָּא 'קְהִלַּת יַעֲקֹב'", עַיֵּין שָׁם,
and in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 9): ''The congregation of Yannai' is not written here, but rather 'the congregation of Yaakov,'' see there,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאַף עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ "בֵּית יַעֲקֹב",
meaning that even simple commoners who are titled 'the House of Yaakov,'
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְרָשׁ בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא לג עַמּוּד ב) "וּלְבֵית יַעֲקֹב",
as expounded in the Gemara (Bava Metzia 33b) on 'and to the house of Yaakov,'
גַּם הֵם יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק בַּתּוֹרָה.
they too possess an intrinsic portion in the Torah.
וְזֶה הָיָה חֵלֶק הָעַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ לְרַבִּי יַנַּאי: "יְרוּשָׁתִי גַּבָּךְ",
And this was the claim of the commoner who told Rabbi Yannai: 'My inheritance is with you,'
שֶׁאַף שֶׁלֹּא לָמַד, רַק פָּסוּק זֶה שֶׁשָּׁמַע וְהֵבִין בּוֹ שֶׁאַף עַם הָאָרֶץ יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק בַּתּוֹרָה.
for even though he had not studied, it was through this single verse which he heard and understood that even a commoner has a share in Torah.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Machshavot Charutz 9:14: “This is the drawing down of “bread from heaven,” like the manna given to those who left Egypt. So it is taught: “The Torah was given only to those who ate the manna.” Yet the Torah was given to all Israel, “an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob,” as that unlearned man said to Rabbi Yannai, “My inheritance is with you.” Necessarily, then, they are all eaters of manna. For the cake they brought out of Egypt had the taste of manna. Consequently, every matzah that commemorates that cake certainly also has the taste of manna. From this comes the nourishment of the entire year, for on Passover judgment is passed concerning grain. Through this bread of poverty, eaten at God’s command, they recognize their poverty and lowliness: they have only what the blessed God gives. Thereby they draw down His bounty and gift, “Who gives bread to all flesh, for His kindness is forever.” All bread is thus found to have the taste of manna. This explains the next verse, “Give thanks to the God of heaven, for His kindness is forever”: although this bread comes from the earth, it takes on the holiness of bread from heaven when one recognizes that the blessed God is its giver.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Simchat Torah 39:2: “Nevertheless, since words of Torah have been apportioned to the entire congregation of Jacob, even to the lowliest soul, someone who is truly a Torah scholar must recognize, through the outward garment of proper conduct that he sees in an unlearned person, the depth and preciousness of the point of Torah within him. This is why the man seized him and said, “My inheritance is with you. It does not say ‘the congregation of Yannai,’ but ‘the congregation of Jacob.’” God has apportioned words of Torah to all the souls of Israel, so that even the lowliest Israelite cannot, God forbid, be wholly without Torah. In the point of Torah found in each individual, that person is truly distinguished and raised above all Israel. He therefore seized Rabbi Yannai and said, “My inheritance is with you”: although I myself do not recognize the words of Torah in the depth of my heart, because I am unlearned, you, Rabbi Yannai, are a Torah scholar. From the proper conduct I possess, you should have discerned and demonstrated the preciousness of the point of Torah within me, from which all that proper conduct branches out. These truthful words awakened Rabbi Yannai. He immediately acknowledged them and regretted what he had said: “All this proper conduct is with you, and I called you a dog!””

p: "וַאֲבָרְכָה מְבָרְכֶיךָ" – חָמֵשׁ, נֶגֶד קְדֻשַּׁת אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן,
''And I will bless them that bless you'—five, corresponding to the holiness of Aharon the Priest,
שֶׁלּוֹ נִיתַּן הַכֹּחַ לְבָרֵךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַאֲנִי אֲבָרְכֵם",
to whom was granted the capacity to bless Israel, as is stated: 'and I will bless them,'
שֶׁמַּשְׁפִּיעַ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַבְּרָכוֹת לַכֹּהֲנִים שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְבָרֵךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
in that Hashem, blessed be He, channels the blessings to the Priests so they can bless Israel.
וְזֶה הַכֹּחַ מֵאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And this power is inherited from Avraham our Father, peace be upon him,
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אַתָּה כֹהֵן לְעוֹלָם עַל דִּבְרָתִי מַלְכִּי צֶדֶק",
and this is what Scripture states: 'You are a priest forever after the order of Malki-Tzedek,'
שֶׁנִּדְרָשׁ (נְדָרִים לב עַמּוּד ב):
which is expounded (Nedarim 32b):

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Divrei Soferim 24:1: “The Sanhedrin are called “the eyes of the congregation,” and the high priest is the head of the community. Likewise, all the holiness of priests and Levites is what emanates and is set apart from the holiness of the children of Israel. Although they were raised above them, this comes through Israel’s holiness, revealed more greatly in the tribe of Levi. This is the meaning of “Take the Levites from among the children of Israel.” Therefore, in the verse “I have given the Levites” in Behaalotekha, “the children of Israel” is said five times. Our Sages said, as cited in Rashi, that the fivefold mention in one verse makes known Israel’s belovedness. Why make it known specifically in that verse? So that we should not think the selection of the Levites from Israel implies a lack in Israel—that only the Levites were chosen for God’s service and all Israel were rejected as unfit for it. Precisely there it makes known their belovedness: the Levites were selected only through the great belovedness of Israel. Because of that belovedness, it was fitting for a tribe from among them to be chosen to serve Him. Without the intense belovedness of all Israel, no Levites would have been chosen at all. Their entire distinction is from within Israel and on account of Israel’s distinction and belovedness.”

p: "וּמְקַלֶּלְךָ אָאֹר" – שִׁית, וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד יוֹסֵף,
''And him that curses you will I curse'—six, and it corresponds to Yosef,
שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם,
whose attribute is the Righteous One, Foundation of the World (Yesod),
וְכָל מַאן דְּאִתְגְּזַר אִקְרֵי צַדִּיק (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, כג עַמּוּד א),
and whoever is circumcised is termed righteous (Zohar II 23a),
וְזֶהוּ כְּנֶגֶד בִּלְעָם שֶׁפָּרַץ גִּדְרוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם בַּעֲרָיוֹת,
and this stands opposite Bil'am who breached the moral fence of the world through sexual licentiousness,
וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ, "זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה" בִּקְדוּשָׁה, יוֹסֵף,
and facing him, 'one corresponding to the other' in holiness, is Yosef,
דְּאִיתָא (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ד):
for it is stated (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4):
יוֹסֵף יָרַד לְמִצְרַיִם וְגָדַר עַצְמוֹ מִן הָעֶרְוָה, וְנִגְדְּרוּ כָּל הַזְּכָרִים בִּזְכוּתוֹ;
Yosef descended into Egypt and fenced himself from immorality, and all the males were preserved through his merit;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר "וּמְקַלֶּלְךָ אָאֹר" עַל בִּלְעָם.
and regarding this it is stated 'and him that curses you will I curse' concerning Bil'am.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Divrei Soferim 23:1: “When a person fences himself in some matter, striving with all his strength against his inclination, by this power he fences all the souls of the Israelite nation in all generations in that matter. Thus the Sages said: Sarah went down to Egypt and fenced herself against sexual transgression, and all the women were fenced through her merit; Joseph went down to Egypt and fenced himself against sexual transgression, and all the males were fenced through his merit. In Sarah’s case one could say that this is because all Israel are her seed and descendants. That does not apply to Joseph. It must therefore be because all Israel are one complete body: when one part is perfected, the entire body is perfected. “They went down to Egypt” means that they entered a trial there, in “the nakedness of the land,” the place where the shell of sexual transgression is most powerful. Fencing against sexual transgression there means depriving that shell of all its strength; through this everyone was fenced.”

It must therefore be because all Israel are one complete body: when one part is perfected, the entire body is perfected. “They went down to Egypt” means that they entered a trial there, in “the nakedness of the land,” the place where the shell of sexual transgression is most powerful. h: In you shall all families of the earth be blessed'—behold, seven

p: "וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ כֹּל מִשְׁפְּחֹת הָאֲדָמָה" – הָא שֶׁבַע,
''And in you shall all families of the earth be blessed'—behold, seven,
נֶגֶד מִדַּת מַלְכוּת שֶׁדָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מֶרְכָּבָה לָהּ,
corresponding to the attribute of Malchut to which King David, peace be upon him, is the Chariot,
וְהוּא שֶׁעַל יְדֵי מִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם בָּא הַהַשְׁפָּעָה לְמִדַּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
in that through the trait of the Righteous One, Foundation of the World, the influx descends to the Knesset Yisrael,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, קעח עַמּוּד ב):
and as written (Zohar II 178b):
"הֵ"א, דָּלֶ"ת הֲוַת בְּקַדְמִיתָא, וּמִדְּאִתְעַבְּרַת בֵּיהּ בְּגַוַּוהּ וְכוּלֵי",
'the letter Hei was originally a Dalet, and once it became impregnated within it, etc.,'
וְהַיְינוּ יוֹ"ד שֶׁל שֵׁם שַׁדַּ"י וְאָז נַעֲשָׂה הֵ"א,
namely the Yud of the Name Shaddai, whereupon it became a Hei,
וְהַיְינוּ דְּכָל מַאן דְּאִתְגְּזַר אִקְרֵי צַדִּיק.
which explains why whoever is circumcised is termed righteous.
וּכְתִיב: "וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ כֹּל מִשְׁפְּחֹת הָאֲדָמָה",
And it is written: 'And in you shall all the families of the earth be blessed,'
שֶׁאַף מֵעוֹבְדֵי כוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת מִי שֶׁיִּרְצֶה לְהִכָּנֵס בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְיָמוּל אֶת עַצְמוֹ וִיקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל הַמִּצְווֹת,
that even from among the nations, whoever wishes to enter Israel, circumcises himself, and accepts the yoke of the commandments,
בְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכֻנֶּה,
shall be titled by the name of Israel,
וְיִהְיֶה בִּכְלַל "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים וְגוֹמֵר".
and will be included within 'And your people are all righteous, etc.'

h: Moshe: it reckoned the first four blessings against the four legs

p: וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חָשַׁב אַרְבַּע בְּרָכוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת נֶגֶד אַרְבַּע רַגְלֵי הַמֶּרְכָּבָה,
And in the holy Zohar it reckoned the first four blessings against the four legs of the Chariot,
וְחָשַׁב שָׁלֹשׁ כְּנֶגֶד יְמִינָא וּשְׂמָאלָא וְעַמּוּדָא דְּאֶמְצָעִיתָא,
and reckoned three corresponding to the right, the left, and the central pillar,
וְהֵם מִדּוֹת חֶסֶד, גְּבוּרָה, תִּפְאֶרֶת שֶׁהָאָבוֹת מֶרְכָּבָה לָהֶן,
these being Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet to which the Patriarchs serve as the Chariot;
וְ"הֶיֵה בְרָכָה" מִסִּטְרָא דְּאַרְעָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְהַיְינוּ מִדַּת מַלְכוּת, כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
while 'and you shall be a blessing' is from the realm of the Land of Israel, which is Malchut, Knesset Yisrael.
וְאַף דִּלְפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְנוּ "וֶהְיֵה בְרָכָה" נֶגֶד מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ,
And even though according to what we wrote 'and you shall be a blessing' aligns with Moshe our Teacher,
אַךְ הַמְּכֻוָּון "וֶהְיֵה בְרָכָה" נֶגֶד מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ שֶׁהוֹפִיעַ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק בַּתּוֹרָה,
the intention is that Moshe our Teacher radiated the blessing that every Jew has a share in Torah,
וְעַל יְדֵי כֵן "וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ כֹּל מִשְׁפְּחֹת הָאֲדָמָה",
and through this 'in you shall all the families of the earth be blessed,'
שֶׁאַף הַשָּׁפֵל שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּמְשַׁל לַאֲדָמָה יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק בַּתּוֹרָה,
for even the lowliest in Israel who is compared to earth has a share in the Torah,
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "מוֹרָשָׁה קְהִלַּת יַעֲקֹב", וְכָאָמוּר;
as is stated: 'an inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov,' and as explained;
אֲבָל הַבְּרָכָה הַמְּיוּחֶדֶת שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד מִדַּת מַלְכוּת שֶׁדָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מֶרְכָּבָה לָהּ,
however, the distinct blessing corresponding to Malchut, to which David is the Chariot,
הוּא "וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ וְגוֹמֵר", כְּמוֹ שֶׁחָשַׁב בְּסִטְרֵי תּוֹרָה בְּרָכָה שְׁבִיעִית,
is 'and in you shall be blessed, etc.,' as counted in Sitrei Torah as the seventh blessing,
וְהַכֹּל אֶחָד.
and all is one unified reality.
